subject: Lyra production: client-side retry surge -> backpressure & temporary mitigations
messages:
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@lyra.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Jones <ben.jones@lyra.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unusual 429/5xx spike from 08:50 — urgent

Tessa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and intermittent 5xx responses from your /v1/generate endpoint starting ~08:50 PDT. Our clients are configured to retry on 429/5xx and unfortunately the retry rate has ramped up quickly; it looks like retry amplification is making the problem worse. We're also seeing request latencies spike above 5s and a number of timeouts on our side.

Attached are ~40 sample request IDs and timestamps (lyra-request-id-list.csv). Can you confirm whether this is an issue on Redwood's side (gateway/backpressure) or if we've misconfigured something on our end? We can throttle retries if you recommend it, but we need a short ETA and immediate mitigation guidance.

--
Amelia Park
SRE, Lyra Inc.
amelia.park@lyra.ai
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@lyra.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual 429/5xx spike from 08:50 — urgent

Thanks Amelia —

We're on it. Opening a short bridge and looping in SRE and infra. Can you please pause any increases to client retry rates and put a short jittered backoff in place while we investigate? That will help us avoid amplification while we triage.

I'll update you within 30 minutes with a next step and ETA.

– Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lyra 429/5xx spike — quick triage notes

Tessa / team —

Quick summary from infra: we're observing a classic retry-amplification pattern. Lyra's traffic shows very low backoff/jitter and a tight retry loop; that, combined with a short-lived gateway queueing event on a set of front-end hosts, is causing increased 429s and subsequent downstream 5xx as queues overflow.

Immediate mitigations I propose (pushing now):
- Apply per-customer ingress cap to 50 rps (temporary)
- Enable fallback routing to quantized model_variant-q1 for new sessions
- Enable host-level 429 throttling policy (short window)

I'll push a config blob to prod (attaching redwood-temp-throttle-config.yaml) — ETA 25–35 minutes for initial rollout to their region. We'll monitor 5xx/429 rates and rollback if it negatively impacts other customers.

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lyra 429/5xx spike — rollout update

Applied ingress cap and host 429 throttle at 09:36 PDT to the Lyra tenant in us-west-2. Initial telemetry: 429 rate dropped from ~5.9% to ~1.2% in the affected window. We're also enabling a routing flag to warm KV cache prefixes for Lyra's active sessions.

Notes / asks:
- Recommend Lyra apply exponential backoff with jitter on their retry logic (we asked them to pause increases, but they need a config change client-side)
- We'll update the public status page once the 5xx tail reduces further

Dylan Brooks
Production Infra
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@lyra.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Jones <ben.jones@lyra.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual 429/5xx spike from 08:50 — urgent

Thanks — we've pushed a client patch to add exponential backoff and jitter and will hold retries at current levels. Appreciate the ingress cap — can you confirm whether we should route production traffic to the fallback quantized model_variant-q1 now or wait until you say it's stable? Also please share the status page link for our ops channel.

Amelia
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@lyra.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: Lyra backpressure mitigation in place

Amelia —

Short status update:
- Mitigations applied: per-tenant ingress cap (50 rps), host 429 throttle, routing to model_variant-q1 for new sessions, and KV-prefix warmup.
- Observable impact: 5xx+429 combined rate dropped from ~6% at peak to ~0.7%; median latency returned to baseline for most traffic.
- Customer action: thank you for applying client-side backoff — please keep retries rate-limited while we stabilize.
- ETA for full remediation & rollback of temporary caps: ~6 hours. We'll follow up with a postmortem and action items.

Public status: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/LYRA-2027-09-01
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7721

I'll keep you posted on progress. If you see a regression, please escalate on this thread or ping me directly.

– Tessa
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Postmortem draft: Lyra 09/01 short-term backpressure event

Team —

I attached a draft postmortem (postmortem-draft.docx) summarizing the root cause (client retry amplification + transient gateway queueing), timeline, and proposed permanent mitigations (better tenant-level admission control, client-safe SDK changes, and improved throttling signals). Please review and add any missing telemetry links or exec-facing bullet points. I'll fold feedback into a version for legal/CS and for the Lyra exec update.

Jonas Weber
Director, Reliability Engineering
jonas.weber@redwood.com
